adjustment: A small change made in response to new information or conditions.
basis point: One hundredth of one percentage point.
benchmark: A reference point used to compare performance, prices or rates.
bond: A debt security that generally pays interest and repays principal on set terms.
A connection that ties people or things together.
To form a close connection or join things together.
bond market: The market in which governments and companies issue bonds and investors trade them.
bond yield: The return on a bond expressed as a percentage, which depends on the way it is measured.
borrow: To take money or something else with an obligation to return or repay it.
capture: To show or convey an important aspect of something.
To catch or take control of someone or something.
case for: Reasons that support doing or accepting something.
central bank: An institution that manages a currency and carries out monetary policy.
central banker: An official responsible for decisions or operations at a central bank.
chalkboard: 黑板；用粉笔书写的牌子
A board used for writing messages in chalk.
consensus: A view that most members of a group agree on.
council: An elected body that makes local government decisions.
A group formally assembled to govern or advise.
cut: A reduction in an amount, a price, or a rate.
To make something lower or smaller, or to divide it with a sharp tool.
demand: To insist on getting something or to require it.
The amount that people are willing to buy at a given price.
delivery driver: Someone who drives a vehicle to deliver goods.
dovish: 偏鸽派的；倾向较宽松货币政策的
Inclined to favour lower interest rates or other support for the economy.
Inclined to favour negotiation over confrontation or military action.
edge: To move or change gradually by a small amount.
The outer limit of something or a slight advantage.
edge higher: To rise slightly, often said of prices or rates.
expectation: A belief about what is likely to happen.
experiment: A test carried out to learn what happens under particular conditions.
financial market: A market where financial assets are issued or traded.
fiscal policy: Government choices about spending, taxes and borrowing.
figure: A number that expresses a quantity or a statistic.
A person, especially a well-known one, or the shape of a body.
fixed-rate mortgage: 固定利率按揭；固定利率房贷
A home loan on which the interest rate stays fixed for the agreed period.
footfall: The number of people going through an area or visiting a place.
The sound of a foot touching the ground.
forecast: An estimate of what is likely to happen in the future.
To estimate what will happen in the future.
hawkish: 偏鹰派的；倾向紧缩货币政策的
Inclined to favour higher interest rates or tighter monetary policy.
强硬的；主张强势应对的
Inclined to favour a forceful response to disputes.
headline: /ˈhedlaɪn/
noun
标题；新闻标题
The title of a news article or the most important items in a news report.
adjective
最受关注的；用于概括主要结果的
Prominent or likely to draw the most attention.
headline result: 最受关注的结果；主要结果
The result that receives the most attention, often a summary measure.
household: The people who live together as a unit in one home.
imply: To suggest something indirectly or make it a likely consequence.
inflation: 通货膨胀；物价总体上涨
An increase in the general level of prices over time.
interest rate: The percentage charged for borrowing money or paid on money saved.
investor: A person or organisation that puts money into assets in the hope of earning a return.
jobs report: A report describing changes in employment and other labour-market figures.
liquidity: The ease of trading an asset, or the ability to meet obligations using readily available funds.
live with: To accept or cope with a continuing situation.
To share a home with someone.
make the case for: 为……提出有说服力的理由
To give a reasoned argument in favour of something.
monetary policy: Central-bank decisions that influence interest rates, credit and the supply of money.
mortgage: A loan secured by property, often used to buy a home.
observe: To watch or notice what happens.
To act in accordance with a custom or rule.
pavement: The paved path for pedestrians along a road in British English.
The hard surface of a road in American English.
pin down: To establish exactly what something is or why it happened.
To hold something in place so it cannot move.
planter: A container for growing plants, often in a garden or public space.
Someone who grows crops, especially on a plantation.
press conference: A meeting where someone makes a statement or answers questions from journalists.
rate cut: A reduction in an interest rate, especially a central bank’s policy rate.
rate hike: An increase in an interest rate, especially a central bank’s policy rate.
recession: A sustained decline in economic activity across a substantial part of the economy.
regulator: An authority or official charged with overseeing an industry or enforcing its rules.
A device that holds a quantity such as voltage or pressure within an intended range.
return: Income or a gain from an investment.
To go back or give something back.
reverse: To undo a change or return to an earlier situation.
To move or cause movement in the opposite direction.
route: The way taken to get from one place to another.
settle: To bring an argument or question to a conclusion.
To make a home somewhere, or to pay what is owed.
shift: To change a position, direction, or opinion.
A change in position or attitude, or a scheduled period of work.
shopkeeper: Someone who owns or runs a shop.
soft landing: A slowdown that brings inflation down without a severe recession.
stock exchange: An organised venue for buying and selling listed securities such as shares.
stock market: The market in which shares in listed companies are bought and sold.
street musician: A person who plays music in a public place, often for tips.
take a longer route: 走一条更远的路线；绕远路
To follow a route longer than an available alternative.
tariff: A duty charged on goods when they cross a customs border.
A schedule of charges for a service.
trader: Someone who buys and sells assets or goods.
traffic light: A set of coloured lights controlling traffic at a junction or crossing.
trial: A limited test to find out how well something works.
A formal examination of a case in court.
uncertainty: A lack of certainty about how things will turn out.
uneventful: 平淡无事的；没有意外的
With no unusual or significant events.
work out: To understand something or find a solution through thought or experience.
To develop in a particular way, often successfully.
yield: The income or return on an investment as a proportion of its value.
To give way under pressure or stop resisting.
To produce something as a result.
The amount produced, for example by a crop.
yield curve: A chart showing bond yields at different maturities for comparable debt.
yield to pressure: 在压力下让步；屈服于压力
To stop resisting because of pressure from others.
